# Is it Better to Apply on Indeed or the Company’s Website?

Learn from a career coach about why it’s better to apply directly through a company website than through Indeed, and why it helps to send a professional follow-up email.

2 years ago
•

3 min read







By
Rohan Mahtani













Table of contents







- Is it better to apply on Indeed or a company website?
- Should you apply on both platforms for the same job?
- How to apply on a company website after finding a job on Indeed Contact HR
- Reach out to the hiring manager
- Send a follow-up email











With a variety of online job boards out there, it can be hard to know the best place to apply for a job. If you find a position posted in multiple locations, is it better to apply through Indeed alone or directly through the company website?

Generally speaking, it's best to apply to a position directly on a company site and to use your Indeed application as a backup. In this article, we'll discuss why direct applications are more likely to be seen by the right people, how to find direct applications from an Indeed posting, and why sending a follow-up email after applying is a good idea.

a quick reference guide exploring whether it is better to apply on Indeed or through the company website
## Is it better to apply on Indeed or a company website?

Applying for jobs directly on a company's website is better than applying through a second-hand platform, whether it’s Indeed , LinkedIn , or Monster. Jobs listed directly on a company website are usually more aligned with the company's ATS and tend to have priority in the application process as they're directly integrated with the company's internal hiring system.

So, simply put, if you can find a direct application on the company website, apply there.

If you can't find a direct posting, or if the company's internal application redirects you to Indeed/LinkedIn, then applying there is fine. But always check the company website first to see if a direct application is possible.

## Should you apply on both platforms for the same job?

It is ok to duplicate your application for the same position as long as it's through a different platform. If applying on Indeed is quick and simple, then it's a great idea to apply there in addition to the company's website. That way, you can ensure your application is received, no matter which platform the recruiters prefer.

Applying on Indeed in addition to your direct application will serve as a backup, in case your direct application goes unnoticed or gets lost in an overcrowded inbox. Indeed also streamlines the application process, so it can be easy to apply to multiple jobs through the platform. Still, you should always research openings on the company website and apply there, too, if you're genuinely interested in the position.

## How to apply on a company website after finding a job on Indeed

When you're interested in a job on Indeed, your first step should be to head over to the company website and look through their careers section to see if the job is also posted there. Generally, you'll find the career section at the bottom of the company homepage or linked through the site directory. Some companies hire solely through online platforms, such as Indeed and LinkedIn, but most replicate their openings on their official website, too.

Once you have found the direct posting, follow the steps outlined on their hiring page, and make sure to send an optimized resume targeting the specific position. Use our Targeted Resume Tool to align your resume with the position and receive personalized feedback on any keywords or skills missing from your resume.


### Contact HR

If you can't find the posting on the company website, consider contacting their HR department. They might be able to provide you with the contact information of someone to whom you can apply directly or offer more details on the opening.

### Reach out to the hiring manager

When applying directly through a company website, don't just send your resume blindly and leave it at that. Find out who the hiring manager is and reach out to them directly to express your interest. You can find email templates and samples here that you can use to ensure your correspondence is polite and professional.

### Send a follow-up email

After applying for a position directly on a company's website, you should send a follow-up email to maximize your application's chances of success. Sending a follow-up email demonstrates a genuine interest in the position and can make your application stand out from the rest.

Your follow-up email should:

- Be concise and professional.
- Reiterate the role you applied for, who you sent your resume to, and when.
- Include a few sentences briefly highlighting your skills.
- Thank the recruiter for their time reviewing your application
If you also applied on Indeed, you can mention that here as well.

# The Difference Between Applying on Company Sites vs Job Boards





Kareem Abukhadra

Nov 26, 2025

5



4



Share





You find a job you’re excited about.

It’s posted on LinkedIn.

It’s on Indeed.

It’s on Glassdoor.

It’s on the company’s own careers page.

Four different places to apply for the exact same role.

Does it matter which one you choose?

Actually, yes.

Here’s what’s happening behind the scenes.

When you apply on a company’s website, your application goes directly into their applicant tracking system.

The ATS they use every day.

The one their recruiters are logged into constantly.

Your resume lands exactly where it needs to be.

When you apply through a job board, it depends.

Some job boards integrate well with company ATS systems.

Your application flows through seamlessly.

But some don’t.

Some job boards collect applications and batch send them.

Some add extra steps that create delays.

Some have their own databases that recruiters have to log into separately.

And here’s the thing.

Recruiters are busy.

They’re living in their main ATS all day.

If your application landed somewhere else, it might sit there longer.

Or get lost entirely.

So here’s the general rule.

Apply on the company website whenever possible.

Go directly to their careers page.

Find the role.

Apply there.

This ensures your application goes exactly where it needs to go.

No middleman.

No extra steps.

No delays.

Now, there are some exceptions.

LinkedIn Easy Apply is tricky.

Some companies use it as their primary application method.

They’ve integrated it with their ATS and they actually review those applications.

Other companies turned it on and forgot about it.

Applications pile up and nobody checks.

How do you know which is which?

You don’t.

So here’s what I recommend.

If a job has Easy Apply on LinkedIn, go find that same job on the company website.

If the company website also has an application, apply there.

If the company website just redirects you back to LinkedIn, then Easy Apply is probably their real process.

Indeed and other job boards work similarly.

Some are well integrated.

Some are not.

When in doubt, go to the source.

Here’s the other problem with job boards.

The listings are sometimes outdated.

A company posts a job.

It goes up on their website.

Indeed scrapes it.

LinkedIn scrapes it.

Glassdoor scrapes it.

Three weeks later, the company fills the role and takes it down from their site.

But the job board listings stay up for another month.

You apply.

You wait.

You never hear back.

Because the job doesn’t exist anymore.

When you apply on the company site, you’re more likely to see accurate, current listings.

Now here’s the real strategy.

Don’t just apply.

Apply on the company site.

Then go to LinkedIn.

Find the recruiter for that company.

Find the hiring manager for that department.

Send them a short message.

“Hi [name], I just applied for the [role] position on your careers page. I’m really excited about [specific thing about the company or role]. Would love the chance to discuss how my experience in [relevant area] could contribute to your team.”

That’s it.

Now you’re not just an application in a queue.

You’re a person who reached out directly.

You’re on their radar twice.

Once in the ATS.

Once in their LinkedIn inbox.

This doubles your chances of getting seen.

Most people just click apply and hope for the best.

You’re going to be more strategic.

Apply on the company site for the cleanest path into their system.

Follow up on LinkedIn to make sure a human actually sees your name.

Same job.

Better approach.

Better results.

One more thing.

If you’re using job boards to search for openings, that’s totally fine.

Indeed and LinkedIn are great for discovering roles.

Use them to find jobs.

Then go apply on the company website.

Best of both worlds.

You get the search power of the job boards.

You get the direct path of the company site.

And you follow up to make sure you don’t get lost in the pile.

That’s the system.

Where you apply matters.

Go direct whenever you can.

# Why Forcing Candidates to Apply on Your Company Site Instead of Indeed is Hurting Your Hiring Efforts





In today’s hyper-competitive hiring landscape, the candidate experience has become a critical factor in attracting top talent. One of the biggest mistakes employers make is requiring job seekers to leave a job board like Indeed and apply on their company website or any external application form. This seemingly harmless step can drastically reduce application completion rates and drive qualified candidates away.

If your job postings redirect applicants to “apply on company site,” you may be losing out on the talent you need. Here’s why it’s a bad idea — and how using Indeed Apply or other one-click application tools can transform your hiring results.

## High Drop-Off Rates Lead to Fewer Applicants

According to SmartRecruiters , 92% of candidates drop off during the application process if it is too long or complex. Redirecting applicants to your website often leads to clunky, time-consuming forms, causing potential hires to abandon the process entirely.

## Longer Applications Deter Top Talent

Research from Indeed shows that applications with 20 screener questions result in a 40% drop in candidates completing the process. When applicants are forced to leave Indeed to start over on your company site, they often encounter long forms or redundant questions, which further discourages them from finishing their application.

## Mobile Users Expect Simplicity

A large percentage of job seekers apply from their mobile devices. Complicated company career sites that aren’t mobile-optimized can frustrate candidates, prompting them to abandon their application. Indeed Apply , however, is mobile-friendly and allows candidates to complete applications quickly and easily from their phones.

## Easy Apply Jobs Get More Engagement

Jobs with Indeed Apply receive 30% more clicks than those requiring candidates to apply on a company website. More clicks lead to more applications, giving you a larger talent pool to choose from.

## Candidates Expect Convenience

Today’s candidates value efficiency. If your competitors are offering easy, one-click applications, and your process requires extra steps, you’re likely losing top talent to companies that prioritize convenience.

## The Solution: Embrace One-Click Application Tools

Switching to Indeed Apply or similar one-click application solutions simplifies your hiring process, improves candidate experience, and boosts application rates. It’s a simple shift that can yield significant results in today’s talent-driven market.

Don’t let your company site become a barrier to hiring success. Make it frictionless and easier for candidates to apply, and you’ll secure the talent you need to grow.
